lines.en: : Sensei! I’m glad I caught you.
: Me too. Now I don’t have to think up a quirky or depressing anecdote to kick things off.
: Also, what do you mean “caught me?” It’s the middle of the school day.
: Yes, but it’s also lunch time. And I was wondering if you’d like to maybe eat on the roof with me today.
: Check back in a few months when the sky is all red and weird.
: If that was a joke relating to the apparent state of the world that I only just found out about the other day, I’m sorry to say I didn’t quite get it.
: That’s fine, Makoto. You’re a genius and talented and amazing and beautiful and you don’t need to know everything to be the perfect girl we all know you are.
: Look at me. I’m nice now.
: Yeah, too nice. And it’s making me extremely uncomfortable.
: I figured if I got it all out of the way now that it would be fine to just speak normally for the rest of the day and not have to worry about complimenting you.
: It’s really impressive how you can still manage to be an asshole while showering me with compliments.
: My bad. There’s just a lot going on right now.
: True. But, on the bright side, none of it matters anymore since we’re all just going revert back to earlier on in the school year anyway! Isn’t that great?!
: Sensei? Isn’t that great?
: Yeah. So great.
: Okay, so maybe I’ve still got a way to go before I catch up to your apocalypse humor. But, I’d be open to hearing you out about how much it’s been weighing you down.
: I might not be able to fully relate, but I can guarantee you there’s a lot going on in my head that I’m still-
: It’s not even about that. It’s about everything else.
: Like what? If you want to talk, now’s the time to do it since everyone else is in the cafeteria.
: Luckily for you, I’ve been in a very talkative mood lately. So go ahead and pull up a chair since you're about to hear my entire life story.
: Or...at least all the parts of it that I can remember.
: It all started one fateful hot boy summer-
: Goodbye!
: Knock times two.
: Who...is there?
: Me! I have arrived.
: And...you are?
: Kaori, what are you doing here?
: I need help sitting on a child!
: You what?
: Hah...Makoto, go eat in the cafeteria with everyone else. We can hang out on the roof tomorrow.
: What? Just like that? You’re going to walk away from me to help some college student sit on a child? Why? And what child?
: Kaori is definitely not a college student. In fact, she might not even be human. So do yourself a favor and stay as far away from us as possible until I tell you it’s safe to come back.
: But-
: Kaori, come on. I have no idea what you’re doing here. But if we’re going to talk, it should be in my-
: ...office.
: Kaori, what do you think you’re doing bringing Nao here? She’s a missing child. Probably. If anyone is looking for her, you could go to jail.
: Today, Nao-chan learns about human school! Where humans go to school! The place where knowledge happens and where Friend lives!
: I don’t live here, I work here. And I figured you’d understand that on account of the ten thousand jobs you have.
: Nao-chan, the outward mouth vibrations that Friend threw up mean that he is glad that we are here!
: No they don’t. Go home.
: But it was difficult enough riding the school-colored landboat and the next one does not arrive for another 7,800 seconds! We have nowhere else to exist!
: Kaori-
: I need help sitting on the child! Tell him, Nao-chan!
: She’s still not talking?
: She does struggle with her mouth muscle, but she is easy to understand when you can see the colors floating behind her tiny human body.
: Great. Then, can you tell me what clear means?
: Clear means special. It is the color or lack of color assigned to you on my talk-machine. But Nao-chan is not clear. She is purple.

: Well, whatever she is, let’s get her into my office. Lunch break will be ending soon and I don’t want to know what any of the girls would think if they saw me with two people who don’t even go here.
: But I have encountered many of your smaller female companions before. At what point will Nao-chan be tall enough to enlist as a Friend-friend?
: Office. Now.
: Ahh! Do not slow-run at such a jogging pace! Your lower meat-tubes are stronger and larger than the ones that belong to us!
Having absolutely no idea what’s going on (yet again), I quickly make my way through the halls before shoving the two trespassers inside.
The one I’m already familiar with has no trouble accepting that she’s done something wrong and presses herself up against my desk.
The other one, however, begins to pick up objects all over the room and observe them.
As you can see...right now, she is particularly fascinated by a mug.
There is nothing in the mug. It’s just a mug.
And it’s such a strange and unnecessary thing to be doing that I’m just going to talk to Kaori while pretending she doesn’t exist.
: I have sat on so many babies recently that I do not know if I will ever sit again, Friend.
: If you’re referring to actually sitting on babies, stop. But if you’re referring to babysitting, I’m not sure what the issue is. Nao barely speaks.
: The tissue is-
: Issue.
: Bless you. But anyway, the tissue is that mothering the hood is difficult no matter what size the hood is!

: Nao-chan may have a small hood, but if I mother it wrong, the fabrics will become loose and she will have no hood at all! Everything is up to me and it makes the “sleep” like a rock but not a sleep rock.
: What you’re saying is that you’re struggling with motherhood and worry that you’re going to do something wrong that might mess up the girl you kidnapped?
: She is the good girl. And so very interested in round things and other things that are not round but also shiny.
: I went as distant as opening the mothering hood book to learn the secrets of the mothermom. But many of the motherers can not come to an agreement on which hood I’m meant to mother. Or mom.
: I do not know what to do, Friend.
: I mean...you can start by...returning her.
: To where? Nao-chan has no family or burgerfriends. And all of the papers that remind her of who she is are as hidden as the Bigfeet.
: Do you mean...Bigfoot?
: Yes. The Bigfeet. Nowhere to be found and without sockpockets.
: It’s Bigfoot, Kaori. Not Bigfeet.
: Is only one of them large?
: No, they’re both-
: Wait, yeah. Why is it called that?
: You non-Kaori humans are so very non-Kaori. If everyone were also a spider, it would make the world a lot easier to understand. But also there would be webs everywhere, which could get sticky.
: Kaori, I don’t know what you want me to do. I have no idea how to help you with Nao and if you can’t take care of her, just find someone else who can.
: Will you accept the role as her fatherdad? The mothering hood book told me to provide one and you’re the only non-chicken cock I know.
: Don’t objectify me in my office. I’m more than just my best feature.
: Your best feature is your pointy chin. It’s so sharp and capable of causing harm to your adversaries.
: I bet it could pop a sphere of thin, air-filled plastic.
: Well, now I’m just self-conscious.
: Sensei, what on earth is going on?! Who was that girl who-
: Wooooow. Cool mug.
: Sensei, what is happening right now? Who is this person? And that person?
: And, before you answer, please just tell me they’re relatives of yours.
: I am Kaori! The Queen of Spiders, Mistress of the Dark, and greatest waitress in Kumon-mi! And the tiny  human with the ceramic coffee-holder is called Nao-chan.
: And you are Sensei’s cousins...correct?
: Hey, remember earlier when I said that a lot has been happening lately? This is what I was talking about.
: So...let me get this straight.
: A mysterious treasure map with nothing but a kanji character on it was taped to your door when you came home from work...
: And so you went on a journey into the forest to find that treasure...didn’t find that treasure...but then proceeded to find her instead...
: And so, instead of reporting a missing person to the police...you kidnapped her...and now you two are peacefully living together as...sisters? Friends?
: They have an eight-foot chicken named John as well.
: Eight and a half. Very big cock.
: And...uhh...Nao-chan was it? You’re okay with all of this? You’re not being held against your will?
: I see...
: Are you seriously just going to ignore the eight foot chicken? Because that should have been pretty alarming.
: At this point, I’m not sure if anything would alarm me. This world is becoming less and less believable every single day.
: And now you know why I’ve been so exhausted.
: Glasses girl, what is your relationship to the burger man? Has he put his fingers in your mouth before?
: Kaori, please never ask that question to anyone again.
: I...uhh...maybe? I can’t really remember, but...it’s possible?
: Why wouldn't you just say no?...
: I bet you can fit many hand-handles in your face opening. Accept this human compliment and tell your teacher-man to become Nao-chan’s fatherdad as thanks for my words of handcouragement.
: You...want him to help you raise the girl you kidnapped? As mother and father?
: Correct!
: Friend is reliable and kind and would make an excellent fatherdad for Nao-chan! She already loves him very much!
: She does?
: What if I promise you all of the cream in the worldglobe? Or free sausage fests for the rest of your life? Or all of the hot meat you could ever want?
: Kaori, I get that you’re worried, but I’m pretty sure Nao will be fine. She’s not a toddler. She’s old enough to, like...function as an actual human for the most part.
: Just focus on teaching her all of the things she doesn’t know for now. Once she starts seeming like less of a kid to you, I’m sure some of those worries will start to fade.
: How come she gets actual advice when all I ever get is inappropriate touching?
: But what if I can not effectively mom? I do not even have a hood. What am I supposed to drape over her head-bone when the coldness comes in?
: Motherhood doesn’t involve an actual hood, Kaori. If you’re that insistent on keeping her, just do what I said and things will work out fine.
: I’m not going to just step in and be her dad, though. That’s weird.
: Is it weird because you did not create her with your sperms?
: You know, maybe our class isn’t so weird after all if this is who you’re talking to outside of it.
: It’s weird because I barely know her and didn’t sign up for a daughter when I already have Ami and a million other girls I’m supposed to be taking care of.
: Wow, are you actually planning on looking after us now? Or are you just saying that to weasel yourself out of this situation?
: You’re not helping, Makoto.
: You want me to help? Here. I’ll help.
: Sensei and I will raise Nao-chan together. That way, you can go back to focusing on...whatever it is you do while not having to worry about her anymore. Easy fix, right?
: Together?...
: Makoto, that might be easy for Kaori, but not us. You can't just sign me up for things like this.
: Why not? We’re basically married already.
: Not by any choice of mine we’re not.
: Does that work for you, Kaori? I can take her back to my house as soon as you leave.
: I DON’T WANT TO LEAVE NAO-CHAN BEHIND! I’LL BE A GOOD MOTHERMOM!!!!
: There. Problem solved.
: Is it really, though?
: For now, at least. It was clear from the start she never wanted to let her go. She’s just overwhelmed and having some doubts about her ability to provide adequate care.
: The thing is, people tend to whip themselves into shape once they’re threatened with the things they love being taken away. So I may have just saved a child. Go Makoto.
: Nao-chan! I am sorry for my momentary head clouds! I am just as lost as you were in the chicken alley! We can help each other become good human females! That is the promise we are making now!
: Thank you for providing the assistance, Friend! We could not have completed this without you!
: Wait, seriously? He didn’t even do anything. I was the one who actually helped. He just stood there and said no to a bunch of stuff.
: Hey, that’s not true. I did say that one thing about teaching her stuff — which I assume Kaori is going to do as soon as she gets home.
: Nao-chan, what do you want to learn?! I will teach you all of the knowledge in the human world in the order you want so long as the alphabet is not that involved in that order!
: Then it is settled! Nao-chan will learn how to read!
: Will you still bring your body to the building we live in?
: You do not have to fatherdad, but you can still make words happen and stroke the giant cock.

: I’ll still come over, Kaori. Just...keep doing your best for the time being. Even if your “best” is entirely inadequate by most childcare standards. Probably. But I guess that’s an issue for another-
: Bless you.
: But I guess that’s a tissue for another day...
Kaori and Nao leave the office, but Makoto makes sure to stay behind and lecture me about getting myself involved with weird people.
The thing is, they’re kind of the ones who got themselves involved with me.
Like...sure, I do call Kaori on occasion. But most of our important interactions have just been me bumping into her somewhere.
Nao is no different.
Well, actually, Nao is entirely different. But the way in which we met isn’t.
They’re just two weird girls I managed to encounter in my long, strange journey through a world that shouldn’t spin.
And I’m sure that world is even stranger for them.
Kaori’s affection has increased to [kaori_love]!
